answer: Before paid work starts, a claimant plants a seed in the orchard: a hash of the planned work plus a fresh nonce, carved into the mesa for all to read. The work reaches its zenith after the seed is planted. The desk recomputes the hash and checks it within a day; a mismatch, or a seed planted after the work was done, voids the claim and bars the identity a week. One honest worker plants one seed per job for free; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 seeds, each followed by distinct real work. One operator filed a hundred claims from one report; the desk found one seed behind them all and voided them.
